A.subject: Physics
A.text: The figure shows a system of two concentric spheres of radii r₁ and r₂ are kept at temperatures T₁ and T₂ respectively. The radial rate of flow of heat in a substance between the two concentric spheres is proportional to
A.sol_text:
In the region between radial distance r₁ and r₂ let us assume a shall of thickness dx at a radial distance x from the centre.

The thermal resistance provided by this shell to the follow of heat is equal to
dR_TH = dx/(k(4πx²))

Where k is the thermal conductivity of the material.
The rate of heat flow through the shell is Q. The same heat flow occurs through all such shells i.e. the net thermal resistance can be calculated assuming the smaller thermal resistances in series.

⇒ R_TH_total = ∫dR_TH = 1/(4πk)∫_{r₁}^{r₂}(dx/x²)

⇒ R_TH_total = 1/(4πk)((r₂-r₁)/(r₁r₂))

As rate of flow = (T₂-T₁)/R_Th_total

The rate of flow will be proportional to (r₁r₂)/(r₂-r₁)

B.subject: Chemistry
B.text: Effective atomic number (EAN) of Mn in the complex [Mn₂(CO)₁₀] is ______
B.sol_text:
EAN of Mn = 36

Solution:

From the structure diagram shown, the complex [Mn₂(CO)₁₀] consists of two Mn atoms bridged by CO ligands in the center, with each Mn surrounded by 5 CO ligands.

For each Mn atom:
- Atomic number of Mn = 25
- Number of electrons from Mn = 25
- Each CO ligand acts as a 2-electron donor
- Number of CO ligands around each Mn = 5
- Electrons donated by CO ligands = 5 × 2 = 10
- Electrons from the Mn-Mn bond = 1 (half of the bond shared between two Mn atoms, or counted as contribution to EAN)

EAN of Mn = Atomic number of Mn + Electrons from ligands + Electrons from metal-metal bond
EAN of Mn = 25 + 10 + 1 = 36

Alternatively:
EAN = Z + (number of electron pairs donated by ligands) + (charge)
EAN = 25 + 10 + 1 = 36
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

A.text: The set of exhaustive values of x satisfying the inequality |x + 1| + |x - 5| > 8 is
A.sol_text:

Solution:
Answer (2)
Given inequality is |x+1|+|x-5|>8 ... (1)
x = -1, x = 5 are critical points

[Number line with -1 and 5 marked]

case (i): if x < -1 and -1 < 5
⇒ x < -1
⇒ x + 1 < 0
⇒ |x+1| + |x-5| > 8
⇒ -(x+1) - (x-5) > 8
⇒ x < -2 ... (2)
Case (ii): if -1 ≤ x < 5
⇒ x + 1 ≥ 0
|x+1| + |x-5| > 8
⇒ (x+1) - (x-5) > 8
⇒ 6 > 8 is meaning less ⇒ X ∈ φ
Case (iii): if 5 ≤ x < ∞
x > -1
⇒ x + 1 > 0
|x+1| + |x-5| > 8
⇒ x+1 + x-5 > 8
⇒ x > 6
Solution set is x ∈ (-∞, -2) ∪ (6, ∞)

A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: If the direction ratios of two lines are given by a + b + c = 0 and 2ab + 2ac − bc = 0, then the angle between the lines is
A.sol_text:
Answer (2)
Solution:
Answer (2)
Here, a + b + c = 0
⇒ a = −(b + c) and 2a(b + c) − bc = 0
⇒ −2(b + c)² − bc = 0
⇒ 2b² + 5bc + 2c² = 0
⇒ (2b + c)(b + 2c) = 0
⇒ 2b + c = 0 and b + 2c = 0
If 2b + c = 0, then a = −(b + c)
⇒ a − b = −(2b + c) = 0
⇒ a = b
∴ a = b and c = −2b
⇒ a/1 = b/1 = c/(-2)
If b + 2c = 0, then a = −(b + c)
⇒ a − c = −(b + 2c) = 0

A.text: If z and ω are two complex numbers such that |2z − 1− i| = √2 and ω = (z−i)/(z−1). Which of the following is true about ω? (where i = √(−1))
A.sol_text:
Hint:
Use |2z − 1 − i| = √2
⇒ |z − ((1+i)/2)| = 1/√2
Which is circle of centre (1/2, 1/2), r = 1/√2
And equation of circle is:
x(x − 1) + y(y − 1) = 0

Solution:
2|z − 1/2 − i/2| = √2
|z − ((1+i)/2)| = 1/√2
⇒ A circle with centre (1/2, 1/2)
radius = 1/√2
(x − 1/2)² + (y − 1/2)² = 1/2
Simplifying we get
x² + y² − x − y = 0
⇒ x(x − 1) + y(y − 1) = 0 ...(i)
ω = (z−i)/(z−1) = (x+iy−i)/(x+iy−1)
= (x+i(y−1))/(x+(y−1)i)
= ((x−1)+iy)/(x+i(y−1)) × (x−i(y−1))/(x−i(y−1))
= ((x(x−1)+y(y−1))+i(y−(x−1)(y−1)))/(x²+(y−1)²)
ω = i((y−(x−1)(y−1))/(x²+(y−1)²))
⇒ ω is purely imaginary
⇒ ω + ω̄ = 0

A.text: If A is a symmetric and B is skew-symmetric matrix both of order n and A + B is non-singular and C = (A + B)^(-1) (A − B), then
A.sol_text:
(A + B)C = (A + B) (A + B)^(-1) (A − B)
⇒ (A + B)C = A − B
C^T = (A − B)^T ((A + B)^(-1))^T
= (A + B) ((A + B)^T)^(-1)
{∵ A^T = A and B^T = −B}
{as |A + B| ≠ 0 ⇒ |(A + B)^T| ≠ 0 ⇒ |A − B| ≠ 0}
= (A + B) (A − B)^(-1)
∴ C^T (A + B)C = (A + B) (A − B)^(-1) (A − B)
C^T (A + B)C = A + B ...(i)
Taking transpose of both sides, we get
C^T (A + B)^T C = (A + B)^T
C^T (A − B)C = A − B ...(ii)
On adding equations (i) and (ii),
C^T (A + B + A − B)C = A + B + A − B
∴ C^T AC = A

A.text: Amit writes a computer program that tests if an integer n ≥ 1 is prime. His friend Vinod edits the code so that if the input is odd, the probability that the program gives the correct output is 52% and if the input is even the probability that the program gives the correct output is 98%. A.sol_text: Note that n is odd with probability (1/2) and even with probability (1/2). The probability the output is correct for one value of n is (1/2)(0.52) + (1/2)(0.98) = 0.75. Thus, the required probability is (0.75)² = 0.5625 = (9/16).
